summary: The Eastern Oklahoma Library System (EOLS) urges the FCC to preserve and modernize the E‑Rate program, arguing that loss of funding would severely degrade rural library connectivity and increase local costs. The Library System argues that eliminating or reducing E‑Rate support would impose significant financial burdens, degrade connectivity, and harm rural communities, and it urges the FCC to preserve current discount levels and Category Two support. The Eastern Oklahoma Library System opposes a nationwide screen‑time rule tied to E‑Rate funding, urges preservation and modernization of the program, and supports specific reforms to consultant oversight and competitive bidding.
